title: American Music Tourism Act of 2025
official_title: To amend the Visit America Act to promote music tourism, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Harshbarger (R-TN) with Rep. Barragan (D-CA) and 10 cosponsors; passed the House and was placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar. A low-cost, bipartisan addition to existing tourism-promotion duties has a reasonable path to Senate passage.
summary: Adds promoting 'music tourism' to the duties of the Commerce Department's travel and tourism office, directing it to identify and promote U.S. music destinations and events.
brief: Amends the Visit America Act to make promoting music tourism a duty of the Commerce travel and tourism office.

top_lines.headline: Music Tourism Promotion
subs: Commerce must identify and promote U.S. music destinations
Covers both domestic and international travel promotion

top_lines.headline: Reporting
subs: New report to Congress every 2 years on travel goals

items.main: Names the Act the “American Music Tourism Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Responsibilities of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism

items.main: Adds promoting music tourism to the duties of the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism.
items.detail: Amends the Visit America Act (15 U.S.C. 9803, 9801). The Assistant Secretary must identify U.S. locations and events important to music tourism and promote both domestic and international travel to them, alongside existing duties for meetings, conferences, and rural and cultural destinations. Adds a report to the Senate Commerce and House Energy and Commerce Committees within one year and every two years thereafter, and defines 'music tourism' as traveling to visit music-related attractions such as museums, studios, and venues, or to attend music festivals, concerts, or other live musical events.

gaps: The bill directs promotion of music tourism but provides no dedicated funding for the new activities.
It defines music tourism and requires reports but sets no measurable target for increasing it.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Harshbarger
featured_quotes.text: We have the opportunity today to vote on legislation centered around something that brings us all together, and that is music. Today, we will take the American Music Tourism Act under consideration. It is a bipartisan piece of legislation that I am proud to have led through the House alongside my co-lead, Representative Nanette Barragan.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Pallone
featured_quotes.text: this bill, as I said, was part of that bipartisan package that we had hoped would be passed last December but for Elon Musk. This bill is important. I know that back in Asbury Park, in particular, they will be very happy to know that our Congress is paying so much attention to American music tourism.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Bilirakis
featured_quotes.text: let me tell you, the speaker on the floor of the House of Representatives in the great State of Florida used to begin his speeches by saying, ``I am fired up.'' I am fired up, Mr. Speaker, because we are going to pass a great bill that promotes America. With the previous bill honoring the 1980 USA Gold Medal hockey team, this is a great day in D.C. and all over the United States of America.

added: 'Music tourism' promotion added to the Assistant Secretary of Commerce's travel duties; biennial report to Congress; statutory definition of 'music tourism' (Visit America Act, 15 U.S.C. 9803, 9801)
